title.narrative: BREAK FREE FAWE Ethiopia

description.narrative: The Break Free! consortium goes with the strategic objective that adolescents exercise their right to live free from teenage pregnancy (TP) and child marriage (CM) supported by civil society. Civil society organizations, youth-led groups and networks will be strengthened to lobby and advocate for improved legislation and implementation to increase girls’ agency and to promote social norm change in favor of the prevention of CM/TP. Three pathways of change have been identified leading towardsthe strategic programme objective: ❖ Pathway 1: Adolescent girls at risk of CM/TP access quality and safe education❖ Pathway 2: Duty bearers and decision-makers develop, resource and implement laws and policies that respond to adolescents’ needs❖ Pathway 3: Adolescents access quality SRHR information, education and servicesTo achieve these outcomes, seven key strategies have been prioritized:1. Social movement/network building2. Capacity building of (youth) civil society organizations (CSOs)3. Network building of (youth) CSOs/NGOs4. Promote access to lobby platforms5. Lobby and advocacy campaigns6. Research7. Learning and exchangeThe geographical focus of the programme is West Africa (Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger), East Africa (Ethiopia, Kenya Sudan) and Southern Africa (Malawi, Mozambique, Zambia). There will also be a programming component at Africa regional level, targeting institutions and other stakeholders operating at this broader level.

youth led CSOs (15 - 25 years old) who report having strengthened lobby & advocacy capacities

In 2024, the six youth-led associations previously established with support from the program continued their active engagement in the program, participating in its implementation. They received refresher training in capacity building to adapt to ongoing contextual changes caused by school closures due to war and conflict in their locality. This training enhanced their resilience and ability to deliver village-based peer-to-peer education. Additionally, the two youth hub centers under YMCA, primarily coordinated by young people, were strengthened, particularly in producing digital SRHR messages. They are now reaching many young people through various media outlets; due to the capacity-building training they received.
The CSOs were involved on different lobby and advocacy activities.

The level of their involvement includes participation in research validation workshops, L&A workshops, Jointly organized national level campaigns, engagement on national level workshops with the house of people representatives.

title.narrative: Number of youth (female) who participate in policy and decision-making bodies who perceive their participation as meaningful

comment.narrative: During the baseline period we have not started engaging youth meaningfully
We didn't have any target for this indicator at the beginning since the baseline was not known.

From the survey conducted among 32 youths, 30 found the participation meaningful (93.8%), including:16 out of 17 female youths (94.1%)14 out of 15 male youth (93.3%). However, the participation of the youth is not as such in the high-level policy and decision-making bodies. The survey assessed their participation in terms of political, policy and decision-making bodies apart from the Break Free! Program in their area or district.
